req.title: Reflect query parameters on GET
req.statement: The system shall include client-supplied query parameters under the 'args' key of the GET /get response body.
expected_outcomes: response args field mirrors query string

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /get must reflect client-supplied query parameters under the 'args' key. I design tests covering: (1) a positive EP case with a single k=v pair asserting exact key and value; (2) a positive EP case with multiple parameters; (3) a negative path with no query parameters asserting args is an empty dict; (4) a BVA boundary case with an empty-value parameter; (5) a DT case verifying that args does NOT bleed into other top-level keys; (6) a NEG case verifying POST /post is a different endpoint and GET /get rejects POST method. Each test uses exact-value assertions to kill constant, operator, and key-name mutations.

tests.name: test_single_query_param_reflected_in_args
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
trace: R-HTTPBIN-002: args key mirrors query string
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json

def test_single_query_param_reflected_in_args():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/get?foo=bar')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = json.loads(r.data)
    assert 'args' in body
    args = body['args']
    assert args == {'foo': 'bar'}
    assert args['foo'] == 'bar'
    assert len(args) == 1

test_single_query_param_reflected_in_args()

trace: R-HTTPBIN-002: all supplied query parameters appear under args
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json

def test_multiple_query_params_all_reflected_in_args():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/get?alpha=1&beta=2&gamma=hello')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = json.loads(r.data)
    args = body['args']
    assert args == {'alpha': '1', 'beta': '2', 'gamma': 'hello'}
    assert len(args) == 3
    assert args['alpha'] == '1'
    assert args['beta'] == '2'
    assert args['gamma'] == 'hello'

test_multiple_query_params_all_reflected_in_args()

tests.name: test_args_key_not_contaminating_other_top_level_keys
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Inspect all top-level keys in response body
expected: Top-level keys are exactly: url, args, headers, origin
x=99 does NOT appear under url, headers, or origin directly
trace: R-HTTPBIN-002: args is the sole reflection point for query params; other keys must not be polluted
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json

def test_args_key_not_contaminating_other_top_level_keys():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/get?x=99')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = json.loads(r.data)
    assert set(body.keys()) == {'url', 'args', 'headers', 'origin'}
    assert body['args'] == {'x': '99'}
    assert body['args']['x'] == '99'
    assert isinstance(body['headers'], dict)
    assert 'x' not in body['headers']

test_args_key_not_contaminating_other_top_level_keys()

def test_post_method_on_get_endpoint_returns_405():

semiflatten helper converts multi-value keys to lists
actions: Send GET /get?k=1&k=2 via test client (same key twice)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-002: boundary — duplicate keys produce list values via semiflatten
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json

def test_duplicate_key_query_params_reflected_as_list():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/get?k=1&k=2')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = json.loads(r.data)
    assert 'args' in body
    args = body['args']
    assert 'k' in args
    assert args['k'] == ['1', '2']
    assert isinstance(args['k'], list)
    assert len(args['k']) == 2
    assert args['k'][0] == '1'
    assert args['k'][1] == '2'

test_duplicate_key_query_params_reflected_as_list()
